mappings.note: Pollination has already happened (pollen is on the stigma, tube in the style); the item asks only what comes next, so it probes the fertilisation half of LO-4, not the pollination half. Not C-3.2-LO-3: nothing is asked about ovule becoming seed.

Seed dispersal is named in only one outcome in the whole frame. The student infers an abiotic agent (wind) from seed structure. Not C-2.8-LO-1, which needs two groups of organisms interacting; a dandelion and the wind are not that.
Classifies the pollination event (cross, because pollen crosses between two maize plants). No agent is named, so C-4.3-LO-1 is not engaged; no fertilisation product is asked about, so not C-3.2-LO-3.

The answer turns entirely on where fertilisation happens (open water versus inside the body), so it is the fertilisation limb of LO-4. Not LO-7 or LO-9: both modes compared here are sexual, so no asexual comparison is in play.
One-step recall of which mode of fertilisation protects the gametes. Same outcome as the sibling item on egg numbers, but this one tests naming the mode rather than its numerical consequence.

POOR FIT. Purely about puberty and adolescence, for which curriculum 82 records no learning outcome on this chapter. C3.2 (life processes including reproduction) is the nearest legal container. LO-10 rejected: its subject is contraceptive devices, not pubertal change.

POOR FIT. Arithmetic on menstrual cycle length. The frame has no menstrual-cycle outcome, so only the parent competency reaches it. Deliberately not LO-10, which covers contraception and reproductive health, not cycle physiology.

Chromosome number in the zygote is a mechanism-of-heredity matter, exactly C3.3's description (DNA, genes, chromosomes). Not C-3.3-LO-5: that outcome is about variation, and this item asks about constancy of chromosome number, which no outcome in the frame states.

Barrier devices and STI protection. LO-10 is the only code in the legal set that reaches reproductive health at all, and it reaches it only because several distinct outcomes (contraceptive devices, population control, reproductive health) are fused into one row.

Compares two contraceptive devices on what each does and does not protect against. The least strained use of LO-10 in the chapter, because both the device and the health consequence are inside the item.
POOR FIT. Parental care and the length of post-natal dependency. No outcome in the frame covers development after birth; the competency is the ceiling.

Emasculation plus foreign pollen forces cross-pollination; the item tests recognising which pollination process was ensured. C-3.2-LO-3 not cited because seeds appear only as evidence that pollination worked, not as the thing explained.

The four stages to be ordered run pollination, germination, fertilisation, zygote, which is precisely the two events LO-4 names. The sequence stops at the zygote, so C-3.2-LO-3 (ovule to seed, ovary to fruit) is not reached.

Tests what follows fertilisation in a human (division in the oviduct before implantation). Mapped to the fertilisation limb of LO-4; the frame records no separate outcome for implantation or the uterine cycle.

The asked-for reason is genetic identity from mitosis with no gamete mixing. LO-7 and LO-9 carry byte-identical text; LO-9 is chosen because its parent is C3.3 (heredity and variation), which is what this item explains. The LO-7 twin under C3.2 is reserved for method and process comparisons.
POOR FIT. Subject is why the menstrual cycle halts in pregnancy. Implantation is only the mechanism quoted in the answer; the thing examined is the cycle, for which the frame has no outcome.

Reasons from what a nocturnal pollinator can perceive, so the plant-pollinator interaction outcome leads; C-4.3-LO-1 added because the answer must name the biotic agent (moths, bats). Contrast the sibling item on insect-pollinated traits, which is pure trait-to-agent matching and takes C-4.3-LO-1 alone.

Disease vulnerability of clones is a consequence of absent genetic variation, so the C3.3-parented twin. Not LO-7, reserved here for items comparing the two modes as processes rather than by genetic outcome.

Asks what happens to genetic diversity when sexual reproduction is restricted to selfing, which is directly how variation is introduced by sexual reproduction. The pollination mechanics are assumed rather than tested, so not C-3.2-LO-4.

Two demands: name suitable methods (vegetative propagation, tissue culture, which is LO-7, the process twin under C3.2) and explain why they work (clones, which is LO-9, the heredity twin under C3.3). The clearest case in the chapter where both twins earn their place.

Part (i) asks the student to frame testable hypotheses, the one thing LO-14 uniquely names; C-3.2-LO-4 because the phenomenon under test is pollen germination. Only two items in the chapter ask the student to generate questions rather than answer them.

Infers pollination type from floral architecture (enclosed stamens, flowers that pollinate before opening). No agent is at issue, so C-4.3-LO-1 is not cited even though other pollination items in this chapter do use it.

The whole case is a plant-pollinator dependency and what happens to yield when it breaks, so C-2.8-LO-1 leads; C-4.3-LO-1 for the role of the biotic agent introduced (bee colonies). LO-14 was considered for the hypothesis sub-part but the item supplies the hypothesis instead of asking the student to pose one.
POOR FIT. Critiques a claim about ovulation timing. Cycle physiology has no outcome in this frame. Not LO-14: the student evaluates a given claim rather than posing a question.

Definitional item, but the distractor set turns on identical copies versus new individuals of their own kind, which is the asexual/sexual contrast LO-7 names, read as a process. Mapped to the C3.2 twin rather than LO-9 because no genetic mechanism is asked for.
